## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The advertised compression figures have different scopes: Elastic documents about 32x smaller quantized vector RAM, while MongoDB documents 32x smaller vector values but about 24x lower vector-index RAM because the HNSW graph remains uncompressed. These figures do not establish an end-to-end memory advantage for either service. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/vector/knn/optimize-performance-accuracy

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] RaBitQ supplies the research lineage and a theoretical distance-estimation error bound, but the original BBQ announcement explicitly lists departures, including no random codebook rotation and different rescoring placement. The RaBitQ theorem should not automatically be attributed to BBQ or Atlas. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12497 · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/better-binary-quantization-lucene-elasticsearch

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] BBQ uses asymmetric scoring: stored document coordinates use one bit, while query coordinates use four bits. This differs from the binary query conversion described for Atlas. (high confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/elasticsearch-bbq-osq-vs-turbo · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md
- [statement] BBQ evolved beyond its launch implementation: Elastic describes per-vector optimized quantization intervals, centroid centering and stored correction terms in its OSQ-backed implementation. Comparisons should identify the Elasticsearch/Lucene version rather than assuming earlier implementations are unchanged. (high confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/optimized-scalar-quantization-elasticsearch · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/elasticsearch-bbq-osq-vs-turbo
- [statement] OpenSearch issue 2805 reports recall@100 of 0.32 versus 0.18 on SIFT-128 and 0.63 versus 0.30 on Cohere-768-1M for Lucene BBQ versus Faiss binary quantization without oversampling. This is an implementation-specific benchmark against Faiss, not evidence that BBQ outperforms Atlas. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-25) — https://github.com/opensearch-project/k-NN/issues/2805 · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization
- [statement] Recall recovery depends on data and candidate depth. Elastic advises measuring recall and latency rather than assuming one oversampling value fits all data; an OpenSearch engineering proposal likewise reports that changing preprocessing changes the candidate depth required by Lucene BBQ. (medium confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/vector/knn/optimize-performance-accuracy · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://github.com/opensearch-project/k-NN/issues/3514
- [statement] VectorDBBench documents Elastic Cloud HNSW_BBQ runs with candidate-count controls and exposes rescoring and oversampling options. It offers a reproducible harness starting point, but its README alone does not constitute a controlled Atlas-versus-BBQ result. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/zilliztech/VectorDBBench · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas automatic binary quantization is documented as mapping each original coordinate above zero to 1 and all others to 0, with the query converted using the same midpoint. BBQ instead centers vectors around a segment centroid and uses correction metadata; the binary-quantization label does not establish algorithmic equivalence. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/better-binary-quantization-lucene-elasticsearch, https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/optimized-scalar-quantization-elasticsearch
- [statement] Both systems retain original vectors on disk for rescoring. Binary candidate retrieval saves working memory, while original-vector reads refine candidate scores and add a separate latency and storage cost. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/vector/knn/optimize-performance-accuracy
- [statement] Evaluate vector-search recall and latency alongside candidate exploration, rescoring depth, vector representation quality and original FP32 vector reads. One-bit storage by itself is insufficient to predict ranking quality. (medium confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/vector/knn/optimize-performance-accuracy · keywords: Lucene BBQ binary quantization compared with Atlas binary quantization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md, https://github.com/opensearch-project/k-NN/issues/3514
